pull_request: Every gate the deploy runs also runs on a pull request, so nothing merges
that main cannot publish. Only a main push or a manual run on main deploys.

Check the brand and the frame against brand.lock and frame.lock

steps.name: Check that no hand-written part was added or grew

#: HW-01, the shrink-only ratchet: this tree and the base revision (the merge
base with main, or main's parent) are measured alike, every producer run
in a scratch copy and every file compared with its pinned upstream; no
file may become hand-written, nor the hand-written total grow.

steps.name: Check that every part fully implements its standards
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -n $BASE ]]; then
  python3 -I tools/standards/gate.py --check --base "origin/$BASE"
else
  python3 -I tools/standards/gate.py --check
fi

#: ST-01 before the slow proof too: every part answers to a registered
standard, and every requirement extracted from each standard's pinned
text is enforced by a suite or listed as debt; on a pull request the
debt may not grow past the base branch's.

steps.name: Name the SDK image digest and the Lean toolchain the proof runs on
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
sdk=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"[^"@]*@sha256:\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock)
lean=$(sed -n 's/^leanprover\/lean4:\(v[0-9A-Za-z.-]*\)$/\1/p' app/lean-toolchain)
test -n "$sdk"
test -n "$lean"
printf 'sdk=%s\nlean=%s\n' "$sdk" "$lean" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#: The proof is the slow part (15 to 25 minutes). This job reuses one
exactly as bootstrap.yml and `just app` do: the cache key only finds a
candidate, and `xtask
proof-reuse` accepts it only if its attestation binds this checkout,
this image's Lean and Lake, the architecture and every input file. A
tag or a manual run proves in full. A reused proof leaves no holo, so
the holo is then built (six minutes, no proof) and must carry the very
build ID the reused attestation verified, or this job fails.
The merge train merges with the workflow's own token, which starts no
push run, so it dispatches this workflow on main instead. That dispatch
stands for the push and is named so here, or every publish would prove
in full (30 minutes, and main's run for #162 was cut at the job limit).
A run a person starts by hand is still a manual run and proves in full.

steps.name: The proof of these exact proof inputs, kept by an earlier page build

with.key: prism-page-proof-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-sdk-${{ steps.proof-inputs.outputs.sdk }}-lean-${{ steps.proof-inputs.outputs.lean }}-${{ hashFiles('app/**', '!app/specs/**', 'prismpm.lock', 'Justfile', 'rust-toolchain.toml') }}

#: This job keeps its own proofs: bootstrap.yml proves inside `just vv`,
and a holo built here never carries the build ID of a proof made
there (seen on main: same inputs, different build). A page proof is
reused only by a later page build, under the same read-time check.
app/specs is not a proof input: the proof reads the lexlean project
(app/src, app/language and app's own files), and a spec reaches it only
through the .lex.tex a generator writes into app/src. So a change to the
specs alone reuses the proof (xtask proof.rs INPUT_PATHS says the same).

steps.name: On main, the proof the merged pull request's page build kept
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
head=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$SHA/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null)][0].head.sha // empty')
test -n "$head"
run=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs?head_sha=$head&event=pull_request&status=success&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
test -n "$run"
gh run download "$run" --repo "$REPO" --name prism-page-proof --dir .prism-proof
echo "candidate proof from the merged pull request's run $run"

#: A cache a pull request saves is never visible to main, so main proved
every merge again (16 to 22 minutes). The merged pull request's own page
build keeps its proof as an artifact; main takes it as a candidate only.
`xtask proof-reuse` still accepts it only if it binds main's checkout,
and any failure here just means: prove in full.

steps.name: Build and verify the holo through the locked SDK
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
image=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock)
if [[ ! $image =~ ^[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?/[a-z0-9./_-]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'prismpm.lock does not select an immutable SDK image' >&2
  exit 64
fi
docker_config=$(mktemp -d)
# The SDK's /tmp is a private directory on the runner's own disk, as
# bootstrap.yml has it since template 1cb0d36: the patched SDK's build
# outgrows a fixed 2 GiB tmpfs.
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$scratch/prismpm-home/.docker"
trap 'rm -rf "$docker_config" "$scratch"' EXIT
printf '{}\n' >"$docker_config/config.json"
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --group-add "$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)" \
  --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
  --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
  --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  --volume "$docker_config:/tmp/prismpm-home/.docker:ro" \
  --workdir "$PWD" \
  --env DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-home/.docker \
  --env BUILDX_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-buildx \
  --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
  --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
  --env PRISM_PROOF_EVENT \
  --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
  "$image" bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail
    # The one way a holo is built when a proof is reused.
    # PrismPM 0.4.0 refuses a provenance statement here: the lock
    # sits at the root, not beside the app. `verify` writes the
    # same holo without one (a487fb6a for #94 both ways), and the
    # build-id check below is what binds it to the reused proof.
    build_holo() { prismpm --project "$1" build --no-provenance; }
    # A pull request proves in full, so main'"'"'s reused-proof build
    # never runs on it. Rehearse that build alongside the proof, on
    # a copy of this tree, so a change that breaks it fails here
    # and not in main'"'"'s deploy (#94 blocked main this way).
    rehearsal=
    if [[ ${PRISM_PROOF_EVENT:-} == pull_request:* ]]; then
      mkdir -p /tmp/rehearsal
      tar --exclude=./.git --exclude=./app/.prism --exclude=./.prism-proof --exclude=./target -cf - . | tar -xf - -C /tmp/rehearsal
      (cd /tmp/rehearsal && build_holo app) >/tmp/rehearsal.log 2>&1 &
      rehearsal=$!
    fi
    just app
    if [[ -n $rehearsal ]]; then
      if wait "$rehearsal"; then
        echo "main'"'"'s reused-proof build works on this tree: $(tail -n 1 /tmp/rehearsal.log)"
      else
        cat /tmp/rehearsal.log >&2
        printf "%s\n" "main'"'"'s reused-proof build fails on this tree, so merging it would block the deploy" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
    fi
    shopt -s nullglob
    holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
    if [[ ${#holos[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
      proved=$(grep -o "\"build_id\": *\"[0-9a-f]\{64\}\"" .prism-proof/verified/manifest.json | grep -o "[0-9a-f]\{64\}")
      test -n "$proved"
      build_holo app
      holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
      test ${#holos[@]} -eq 1
      built=$(basename "$(dirname "${holos[0]}")")
      if [[ $built != "$proved" ]]; then
        # Not the build the reused proof verified: that proof says
        # nothing about this holo, so prove this tree in full.
        printf "the holo built here (%s) is not the build the reused proof verified (%s): proving in full\n" "$built" "$proved" >&2
        rm -rf app/.prism .prism-proof
        PRISM_PROOF_EVENT= just app
        holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
        test ${#holos[@]} -eq 1
      else
        echo "the holo is build $built, the build the reused proof verified"
      fi
    fi
  '

steps.name: Keep the proof for main

#: The proof this pull request ran on, for main to take when it merges.

steps.name: Find the holo
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob
holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
if [[ ${#holos[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
  printf 'expected one holo, found %d\n' "${#holos[@]}" >&2
  exit 64
fi
fingerprint=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")).archive_fingerprint)' "$(dirname "${holos[0]}")/application/holo-identities.json")
{
  echo "path=${holos[0]}"
  echo "fingerprint=$fingerprint"
} >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

steps.name: Sign the holo's provenance as this repository's workflow

if: Only a build that is published is signed. A pull request's page links
its run instead, and is never deployed.

steps.name: Assemble the page
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
cp "$HOLO" site/app.holo
cp -r try/vendor site/vendor
rm -rf site/vendor/prism-code/fixtures
rm -rf site/vault/test
# The page says where this holo's provenance is: the signed statement
# GitHub keeps for the build that made it.
node -e '
  const { readFileSync, writeFileSync } = require("node:fs");
  const [id, url] = process.argv.slice(1);
  const app = JSON.parse(readFileSync("site/app.json", "utf8"));
  app.attestations ??= {};
  app.attestations.build = { id, url };
  writeFileSync("site/app.json", `${JSON.stringify(app, null, 2)}\n`);
' "$FINGERPRINT" "$ATTESTATION_URL"
node bootstrap/page.mjs site
# Every pinned object set (R4's engine and weights, R4-01, and any
# other `bootstrap/*-objects.mjs`), fetched from its pinned commit and
# served as SHA-256-named pieces under the 16 MiB limit. A new set is
# served, and checked below, without editing this workflow.
for objects in bootstrap/*-objects.mjs; do
  node "$objects" site
done
node bootstrap/precache.mjs site

steps.name: No personal data in the assembled page (PV-01)
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
cargo run -q --locked -p xtask -- audit-pii site

steps.name: A first visit's weight, counted once the page has started (FR-03)
Every browser acceptance under test/, from the pieces this page serves
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
export NODE_PATH="$(npm root --global)"
shopt -s nullglob globstar
runners=(test/*/run.mjs)
suites=(test/**/*.test.mjs)
test ${#runners[@]} -gt 0
test ${#suites[@]} -gt 0
for runner in "${runners[@]}"; do
  echo "::group::$runner"
  node "$runner"
  echo "::endgroup::"
done
# Twice, on pull requests and before deploys alike: a check that does
# not decide the same way every run (a race with the page) fails here,
# on its pull request, instead of on main after the merge.
# A time measure is taken with the machine to itself: the suites the product
# record names as gates of its time behaviour measures run one at a time,
# apart from the rest, which run side by side and would slow them.
mapfile -t timed < <(node --input-type=module -e 'import { load } from "./tools/specs/record.mjs"; console.log([...new Set(load("app/specs/product/spec.json").quality.filter((q) => q.subcharacteristic === "time behaviour").flatMap((q) => q.measures.map((m) => m.gate)))].join("\n"))')
rest=()
for suite in "${suites[@]}"; do [[ " ${timed[*]} " == *" $suite "* ]] || rest+=("$suite"); done
for pass in 1 2; do
  echo "::group::every *.test.mjs, pass $pass of 2"
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 "${timed[@]}"
  node --test "${rest[@]}"
  echo "::endgroup::"
done

#: Every browser acceptance under test/ runs here, on every pull request
and before every deploy: each `test/<suite>/run.mjs` (R4-01 and the
rest) and every `*.test.mjs` (PG-01 and the rest). A new suite is in CI
the moment it is committed; none runs only on someone's machine.

steps.name: Check out the exact event revision
Rebuild each stale guest in the locked SDK
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
stale=$(python3 -I tools/guests/gen.py stale)
if [[ -z $stale ]]; then
  echo "every decision guest is current"
  exit 0
fi
echo "stale: $stale"
SDK=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock) tools/guests/build.sh $stale
python3 -I tools/guests/gen.py check
git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | cut -c4- >"$RUNNER_TEMP/rebuilt"
tar -cf "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-guests.tar" -T "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebuilt"
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-guests"
tar -xf "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-guests.tar" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-guests"
echo "rebuilt=true" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
{
  echo "## Stale decision guests rebuilt"
  echo
  echo "Bring them in with \`gh run download ${{ github.run_id }} -n stale-guests --dir .\` and commit:"
  echo
  sed 's/^/- /' "$RUNNER_TEMP/rebuilt"
} >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

steps.name: Hand back the rebuilt guests
Check out the exact event revision
Is this commit still newer than the live page

#: Publishes run one at a time: a newer run may have published while
this one waited, and then this older page must not replace it.

steps.name: Deploy
The published page works (PG-01, live)
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
npm install --no-audit --no-fund --global playwright@1.56.1
playwright install --with-deps chromium
for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
  NODE_PATH="$(npm root --global)" node --test test/page/card.test.mjs test/page/person.test.mjs test/page/returning.test.mjs && exit 0
  sleep 30
done
exit 1

#: The published page itself, in a real browser: it keeps, refuses while
halted and answers through the app, and its owner's walk (CO-01) holds:
content in, every place lists it, Today and Ask answer from it. Pages can take
a minute to serve the new bytes, so the check gets four tries.

steps.name: The published page keeps every working journey and keeps the system view off the screen (PD-01, PD-02, live)
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
for attempt in 1 2; do
  NODE_PATH="$(npm root --global)" node --test test/product/screen.test.mjs test/product/journeys.test.mjs && exit 0
  sleep 30
done
exit 1

#: The product holds on the page the person opens: every journey recorded
as working still works, fresh and returning, and no system word shows
beyond the listed debt. Its scoreboard goes to this job's summary.

guests: A decision change is a spec change: a pull request whose decision guests
are older than their modules gets them rebuilt here, in the locked SDK the
proof uses, as the artifact `stale-guests` laid out at its repository
paths. `gh run download <run> -n stale-guests` and a commit bring them in,
so no one needs the SDK image locally. GU-01 (tools/guests/gen.py check)
still fails until they are committed.

name: Publishes the repository's app page: `site/` with the holo that `just app`
builds and verifies through the locked SDK. Project content, not universal
policy: a repository may extend or replace it.
It runs on every push to main, beside `bootstrap`, not after it: `just app`
is the proof-bearing build (the Lean kernel checks every theorem before the
holo exists), so the page goes live as soon as that passes, while the rest of
the gate runs on both architectures. The SDK step and the signing step are
the ones `build.yml` runs, copied here: the gate pins every `uses:` to a
commit and so forbids calling a workflow by path. When `build.yml` changes
either step, copy it again. The page then carries the same holo that
`prism-code build --remote github` would hand a device, with the signed
provenance of the run that made it beside it.
concurrency: A newer push to a pull request cancels its older run. Main's gates run as
soon as each merge lands, beside each other (a queued merge waited 12 to 27
minutes for the one before it); only the publish job is one at a time, never
cancelled, and it publishes only main's head, so an older run that finishes
later never puts an older page back.
